method: leaf physiognomy (foliar physiognomy vs modern database) + MAT lapse rate
reference_short: Gregory-Wodzicki et al. 1998 J S Am Earth Sci
notes: Abstract: flora dated 10.66+/-0.06 Ma grew at 590-1610 +/-1000 m; present elevation 3940 m. elev_m is the midpoint of the published 590-1610 m range (ours). lo/hi add the stated +/-1000 m error, lower bound floored at sea level (terrestrial flora). Coordinates approximate (Corocoro area), not given in abstract. Classic support for large post-10 Ma uplift; physiognomic MAT-to-elevation conversion assumes a terrestrial lapse rate and global-climate correction.

material_or_proxy: literature-derived sample of fossil dicot leaves (MAT 21.5-21.7 +/-2.1 C)
reference_short: Gregory-Wodzicki et al. 1998 J S Am Earth Sci
notes: Abstract: early-middle Miocene Potosi flora grew at 0-1320 +/-1000 m; present elevation 4300 m. Age given only as early-middle Miocene; age bounds here are the epoch limits (ours). elev_m is the midpoint (ours). Weak because the leaf sample is literature-derived and the age is poorly bracketed.

method: nearest living relative (palynoflora; lower cloud-forest limit)
reference_short: Graham et al. 2001 Am J Botany
notes: Abstract: locality at 3600 m today; flora indicates lower limit of cloud forest, ~1200-1400 m, with an error of at least +/-1000 m; maximum age ~6-7 Ma (Miocene-Pliocene boundary). Age interval here is that maximum age down to the base of the Pliocene (our reading); the flora may be younger. Authors infer one-third to one-half of Eastern Cordillera uplift had occurred by the start of the Pliocene. Weak because only a maximum age is available.

site: Corque syncline / Callapa section, northern Altiplano, Bolivia
method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry with local d18O-altitude gradient
notes: RELATIVE: abstract states surface uplift of ~2.5-3.5 km between ~10.3 Ma and 6.8+/-0.4 Ma, when the Altiplano reached its current elevation; so before ~10.3 Ma the basin stood 2.5-3.5 km below its present elevation (~3.8-4 km modern Altiplano surface, i.e. roughly 0.3-1.5 km; arithmetic ours, not stated in abstract). Corroborated by Ghosh et al. 2006 Science (10.1126/science.1119365; Delta47 paleosols, 1.03+/-0.12 mm/yr between ~10.3 and ~6.7 Ma). 'Rapid rise' interpretation contested by the 'slow and steady' school: Ehlers & Poulsen (2009) argue part of the d18O and temperature shift reflects climate change once threshold elevations were crossed.

site: Corque syncline / Callapa section, northern Altiplano, Bolivia
method: stable isotope (d18O) paleoaltimetry with local d18O-altitude gradient
notes: NEAR-MODERN: abstract states the Altiplano rose to its current elevation by 6.8+/-0.4 Ma; compare with present-day surface (~3.8-4 km). Same rapid-vs-gradual debate as the pre-10.3 Ma row.

material_or_proxy: paleosol carbonate Delta47 and d18O; pollen
notes: Abstract: northernmost plateau remained at low elevation (0.9+/-0.8 to 2.1+/-0.9 km) until ~9 Ma, ~15 C warmer than present. Older age bound of the record not given in abstract (abstract not fully accessed for section ages). elev_m midpoint of the two central estimates (ours); lo/hi span the stated errors. Coordinates are the northernmost Altiplano basin area, approximate.

Abstract: modern elevations of ~4 km reached only by ~5.4 Ma, from a shift in leaf-wax dD. No error stated in abstract. Authors infer south-to-north progressive uplift (south 16-9 Ma, north and central 10-6 Ma).
Abstract: Oligocene-early Miocene (29-24 Ma) paleoelevations 0-1.5 km a.s.l. elev_m midpoint (ours). Sections not named in abstract; coordinates are an approximate Eastern Cordillera centroid.

material_or_proxy: paleosol carbonate (Delta47 temps 15-23 C at ca. 17 Ma)
notes: Abstract: middle Miocene (ca. 20-15 Ma) paleoelevations ~2.5 km a.s.l.; rise of ~1-2.5 km between ca. 24 and 15 Ma attributed to removal of dense lower lithosphere without upper-crustal shortening. Point estimate, no error in abstract.

site: Western Cordillera basin, southern Peru (northern plateau)
method: stable isotope (dD) of hydrated volcanic glass
notes: NEAR-MODERN: abstract states the basin reached its current elevation by 16 Ma after 2.2-3.7 km of punctuated uplift between 19 and 16 Ma (2.2 km with modelled isotope-climate change, 3.7 km with static modern climate), >6 Myr earlier than the central plateau; very negative dD persists into the Pliocene. Basin not named in abstract; coordinates approximate.

site: Puna Plateau (Salar de Antofalla, Salina del Fraile, Arizaro Basin)
method: stable isotope (dD) of hydrated volcanic glass
notes: Abstract: elevated (~4 km) Puna since ca. 36 Ma with limited (<1 km) change since; no large Miocene uplift unlike the Altiplano. lo/hi encode the stated <1 km change (our reading). Weak: Eocene glass hydration age and moisture-source assumptions are debated, and Quade et al. 2015 (10.1130/2015.1212(15)) report that clumped-isotope paleothermometry in this region failed through burial resetting, leaving glass dD and evaporite distribution as the main constraints. Coordinates are a centroid of the three basins (24-26 S).

material_or_proxy: carbonate nodules; marlstone; spring deposits; volcanic glass
notes: NEAR-MODERN: abstract states the Puna was near its present elevation since at least ~10 Ma, while the Eastern Cordillera of NW Argentina rose ~1.5 km between ~14 and ~7 Ma. No numeric elevation in abstract; coordinates approximate.
